topics.label: Start
topics.title: Start investigating
paragraphs: You are an independent investigator working from the WHOAMI desktop. Read the client's message first, then follow the evidence across the available apps.
Search records, compare sources, and build a timeline. A useful conclusion should be supported by several independent pieces of evidence.
The desktop is a simulation: your commands only affect this case and never run on your computer or contact real services.

items.description: Select an app in the dock to open it. Drag windows by their title bars; minimize, maximize, close, or resize them with the window controls.
Keyboard: 1–9 and 0 open the dock apps in order, Esc closes the active window (press it once more if you are typing in a field).
Open Handbook from the dock to return to these instructions. Mail is where every case begins.
Start with what is already available, then follow names, dates, accounts, locations, and other details into related records.
Evidence may be public, found in an app, or locked behind a simulated account or target. Keep track of what you have discovered and downloaded.
Every record you find lands on the Evidence board automatically, with a NEW EVIDENCE notice at the top of the screen.
Drag a card title onto another card to connect them with a thread; remove a thread at any time.
Use Add to report on evidence cards to choose which records support your final report.

topics.label: Terminal
topics.title: The case terminal
paragraphs: The terminal is a simulated command interface for the fictional case. It does not provide access to your computer, the internet, or real systems.
Type a command and press Enter. Use the up and down arrows to recall previous commands. The terminal history and investigation progress are saved for this case.

topics.label: How to hack
topics.title: Unlocking simulated records
paragraphs: Some fictional records require a simulated access path. Follow the requirements shown by the case; not every record uses every step.
A target only matters once you know what to look for on it: a profile you opened, an account, a number from another record. Leads come first.

items.description: List the targets you currently have leads for.
Connect to the case's fictional VPN node when a target requires it.
Inspect a target: its steps, and how many of its records you have leads for.
Connect to a scanned target after meeting its requirements.
Save the records made available by the connection.

After the archive is unlocked, use unzip <archive> to extract its records.

topics.label: Passwords
topics.title: Finding passwords and clues
paragraphs: Passwords are part of the investigation. The handbook does not contain case passwords: look for clues in evidence, messages, public posts, and account records.
A clue may point to a meaningful word, date, or combination. Treat it as a lead and verify it against the evidence rather than trying unrelated guesses.

items.description: Use login with the service, account, and password supported by the case records. A failed login means the credentials or account do not match.

For encrypted archives, add discovered clues to your wordlist and run crack with --wordlist mine. Each clue is tried on its own and joined with one other clue; only clues you collected in-game are checked.
Once an archive is unlocked, extract it with unzip. Its contents then become available in Files.

topics.label: If stuck
topics.title: If you are stuck
paragraphs: Nothing in a case is random. When the trail goes cold, go back to what you already have and read it again, slowly.

items.description: Re-read the client's message and its attachments. Names, emails, devices and times are all leads.
Search the Database by name, phone, address or plate. Opening a dossier can reveal new terminal targets.
Shows which targets you have leads for. scan <target> shows which of its records you still can't reach.
Search the Browser with exact words from the evidence: handles, places, dates, phone numbers.
Check Mail. New messages arrive as the case moves.
Open the Map: places, towers, the phone route and cameras appear as you find evidence. Compare where people were with when.
Write down the official timeline, then check each step against an independent record. Where two sources disagree, one of them is wrong.
Look for things that should be there and aren't: steps, signals, witnesses, activity.
An alibi is a record too. Check its time and place as carefully as anything else.
